title: Ordinary open localization kernel equals recorded compact support
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a field k in which l is invertible. Let X be a separated finite-type k-scheme, i:Z→X a closed immersion and j:U→X its complementary open immersion over k. For an integral constructible object K [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], assume its recorded integral j-pullback is constructible. The termwise derived functor of the literal kernel of the closed unit [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data], evaluated on K, is isomorphic to the underlying recorded integral compact-support value for (j,id) of that pullback [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. This asserts only an object comparison, not preservation, linearity, or a distinguished triangle.

source.place: The triangle, integral coefficient case; Constructibility, first paragraph

proof.text: Use the actual coefficient inverse-image maps. The ringed open/closed sequence identifies the kernel of the closed unit with open extension after ordinary restriction, including its kernel inclusion. Pass this exact natural identification to derived categories.

Identify ordinary immersion restriction of complete K with the recorded completed integral pullback through the completion-unit-normalized comparison. Transport the coefficient presentations and their finite quotient maps, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

Exact open extension preserves countable products and Roos triangles. The strict open reduction comparison identifies the full finite reduction tower and every transition with the compact-support tower for (j,id). Thus the ordinary open value is the Roos limit of that tower.

The normalized recorded compact-support realization is the same limit. Rotate the two distinguished Roos triangles and extend the identity on their two product vertices; two-out-of-three gives the vertex isomorphism. This includes zero K and empty U.

proof_origin.place: The triangle, integral coefficient case; Constructibility, first paragraph

theorem sfIntegralOpenKernel_compactSupport
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : IsUnit (l : k))
    {Z U X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [U.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [j.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X)
    (h : sfIntegralConstructible l E U ((integralDerivedPullback l E j).obj K.obj)) :
    letI := sfRecollementNoetherian k X
    letI := (sfRecollementOpenFiniteType k j).1
    letI := (sfRecollementOpenFiniteType k j).2.1
    letI := (sfRecollementOpenFiniteType k j).2.2
    Nonempty ((sfRecollementModuleOpen l E i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj ≅
      (sfIntegralCompactSupportValue l E k hk
        (Compactification.ofIsOpenImmersion j) ⟨_, h⟩).obj)
